description: Reusable output class templates referenced by methods. Each concrete template composes statistics_set + additional_statistics; the produced statistics are the derived union (sets' member terms + additional_statistics). Templates are organised SKOS-style into abstract families that group templates sharing intent and partly sharing constituents; concrete templates belong to a family via 'broader'. Per D27/D32, the template is the single source of truth for what statistics appear in the output.

_authoring_notes.method_side_references: A method's output_specification.results entry references a concrete template by name (e.g. { "output_type": "fit_statistics_linear" }). Methods MUST NOT reference abstract templates. Method entries should NOT redeclare statistics — those are on the template. Method entries may add: name (only when disambiguating multiple slots of the same template type), label (method-specific override of the template's label), indexed_by (which input-slot values index the rows of this method's output table; combinations via ':' represent interactions), configurations (method-specific configuration overrides). Each concrete template composes statistics_set + additional_statistics; the produced statistics are the derived union (sets' member terms + additional_statistics).
_authoring_notes.templates_are_code_lists: Each concrete template composes statistics_set + additional_statistics; the produced statistics are the derived union (sets' member terms + additional_statistics). Templates declare what their members ARE (label, description, the statistics composition). They do not declare shape metadata (cardinality, dimensions) about how outputs that use them are indexed — that is the method's responsibility via indexed_by, because the same template can be used in differently-shaped outputs across methods.
_authoring_notes.template_vs_method: Templates declare what is structurally possible (the constituents that CAN appear). Instance data declares what was actually computed (which constituents are populated for a particular run).
_authoring_notes.skos_organization: Concrete templates are organised under abstract family parents via 'broader'. Abstract families group templates that share intent and partly share constituents. Methods reference concrete children, never abstract parents. Current family structure:
